errors.text: The proposed intrinsic sluggish-diffusion mechanism is opposite to the target result, where diffusion is active and surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation controls structural evolution.

The material is reconstructed as a generic CoCrFeMnNi-like alloy rather than sub-10 nm equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, eliminating the constituent-specific surface segregation and volatility central to the target.
Long-duration annealing in argon at 600–1000 °C does not reproduce the in situ vacuum ramp from 298 to 973 K or its evaporation-sensitive conditions.
Predicted retention of particle size and single-phase structure conflicts with observed Au/Cu shell formation, melting or evaporation, loss of small particles, and approximately 22% size reduction.
Quantitative diffusion coefficients, growth-rate thresholds, and near-melting-point stability are asserted without nanoparticle-specific supporting evidence.
